selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.

plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests a Fabry-Perot narrowband transmission filter design using recalled thin-film optics principles. The hypothesis is that a symmetric cavity structure with distributed Bragg reflector mirrors on both sides of a half-wave defect layer will produce high transmittance at 1550 nm while suppressing adjacent bands. This route uses no retrieved literature - all design choices come from the model's prior knowledge of interference filter design patterns. I would have wanted to look up: exact refractive indices of Ta2O5 and SiO2 at 1550 nm, typical deposition stress for these materials, and published examples of similar LiDAR filter stacks to validate the layer count estimate.

routes.title: Fabry-Perot Narrowband Transmission Filter for 1550 nm LiDAR
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A symmetric Fabry-Perot cavity with quarter-wave Bragg mirrors surrounding a half-wave defect layer will achieve peak transmittance at 1550 nm while creating stopbands at 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm, with performance improving as mirror pair count increases up to the 30-layer constraint.
routes.design_principle: Recalled thin-film optics: alternating high/low index layers at quarter-wave optical thickness create a photonic bandgap. Inserting a half-wave defect layer in the center creates a transmission resonance within the stopband. The number of mirror pairs controls stopband width and depth; the defect layer thickness controls the resonance wavelength.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | (Ta2O5/SiO2)_7 | Ta2O5 | (SiO2/Ta2O5)_7 | Fused Silica substrate - 29 layers total: 14 mirror pairs plus 1 defect layer, starting with high-index layer from air side
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 29 layers
defect layer thickness specifically tuned for 1550 nm resonance
manufacturing_considerations: total layer count fixed at 29 to stay under 30-layer limit
quarter-wave layers should be near 100-300 nm thickness range at 1550 nm for practical deposition
theory_basis: Recalled: Quarter-wave stack reflectance increases with number of layer pairs, approximately R = ((nH/nL)^(2N) - 1) / ((nH/nL)^(2N) + 1) for N pairs
Recalled: Fabry-Perot transmission peak occurs when defect layer optical thickness equals integer multiples of half-wavelength
Recalled: Stopband width scales with refractive index contrast ratio nH/nL
Recalled: Ta2O5 has higher refractive index (~2.1-2.2) than SiO2 (~1.44-1.45) at 1550 nm, providing good contrast for Bragg mirrors
Recalled: Symmetric mirror structure around defect layer produces cleaner transmission profile than asymmetric designs
expected_advantages: High peak transmittance achievable with sufficient mirror pairs
Well-defined stopbands on both sides of 1550 nm
Symmetric design simplifies optimization and reduces sensitivity to thickness errors
All 29 layers can be individually tuned during optimization rounds
known_risks: Ta2O5 refractive index value at 1550 nm is recalled as approximately 2.1-2.2 but exact value uncertain - registry dataset will provide measured data
SiO2 refractive index recalled as ~1.44-1.45 at 1550 nm but exact value uncertain - registry dataset will provide measured data
7 mirror pairs per side may not provide sufficient stopband depth for 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm suppression - may need to verify if 29 layers is enough
Angle of incidence not specified in request - assuming normal incidence (0 degrees) but LiDAR receivers may have finite field of view
Polarization not specified - design assumes unpolarized or normal incidence where polarization splitting is minimal
Exact passband width around 1550 nm not defined - optimization will naturally determine bandwidth based on mirror pair count
Material absorption in Ta2O5 at 1550 nm not accounted for in recalled knowledge - extinction coefficient data from registry will determine if this matters
routes.execution_request_english: Design a planar multilayer dielectric filter for 1550 nm LiDAR receiver. Incident medium is Air. Substrate is Fused Silica. Use exactly 29 layers with materials Ta2O5 (Gao) and SiO2 (Lemarchand). Stack structure: Air | (Ta2O5 (Gao)/SiO2 (Lemarchand))_7 | Ta2O5 (Gao) | (SiO2 (Lemarchand)/Ta2O5 (Gao))_7 | Fused Silica. Optimize all 29 layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance at 1550 nm while minimizing transmittance in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm bands. Wavelength bands for evaluation: 1400-1500 nm (suppression), 1550 nm (transmission peak), 1600-1700 nm (suppression). Normal incidence assumed. Total layer count fixed at 29. Materials: Ta2O5 (Gao) (high index), SiO2 (Lemarchand) (low index).

valid_candidates should remain high throughout optimization if thickness bounds are physically reasonable
tightest_margin should not decrease significantly across rounds if the symmetric design is robust
transmittance at 1550 nm should show a clear peak distinct from the suppression bands
suppression band transmittance should decrease as mirror pair effectiveness increases with thickness optimization
